title: Standby Power (Vampire Load) Detection
dataSources: Zigbee2MQTT device reports (`zigbee2mqtt:device`), Shelly/Tasmota telemetry (`shelly:status`, `tasmota:sensor`), Hue events (`hue:event`), thermostats (`ecobee:thermostat`).
app: Philips Hue, smart plugs (Tasmota/Shelly/TP-Link Kasa), thermostats (Nest/Ecobee), locks, and Zigbee/Z-Wave sensors via MQTT / Zigbee2MQTT bridged to HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=shelly:status power_w>0
| stats min(power_w) as standby_w, max(power_w) as peak_w by device_name
| where standby_w>2 AND standby_w<peak_w*0.1
| eval annual_kwh=round(standby_w*24*365/1000,1)
| sort - annual_kwh
description: Detects devices that keep drawing power even when idle and estimates the yearly cost of that standby draw.
value: Vampire loads can add up to a noticeable chunk of a power bill; quantifying them per device justifies a smart plug or a switched socket.
implementation: Bridge per-device power readings; schedule weekly and target the biggest standby loads for switching off.
visualization: Table of devices by estimated annual standby energy.
grandmaExplanation: It finds gadgets that keep sipping electricity even when switched off, and shows how much that wastes each year.
